Architecture.label: 01 — Architecture
Architecture.title: Engineering, not decoration.
Architecture.intro: Every pixel is a tolerance, every frame a commitment. High-ROI digital ecosystems are built here in two layers: a front end that feels calibrated, not merely quick, and enterprise automation engineered to fail safely.
Architecture.c1Title: Video, not code. Cinema, in the browser.
Architecture.c1Text: We left heavy render engines and stuttering animation layers behind. Your hero and showcase streams are served as native MP4/WebM video, decoded by the device’s own video hardware, so the stream costs the processor little.
Architecture.c1Tags: H.264 · VP9 · Loads on demand · Space reserved, no layout shift
Architecture.c1VideoLabel: A glass monolith turning slowly on a black background
Architecture.c2Text: Scrolling and transitions follow the display’s own frame rhythm. On desktops with a mouse or trackpad, Lenis eases the scroll; touch devices keep their native, immediate scroll. The page moves like an extension of your hand, not under it.
Architecture.c2Tags: Lenis smooth scroll · requestAnimationFrame · GPU-composited transforms
Architecture.c2Caption: Measured while scrolling on a 60 Hz display. {profile}. {date}.
Architecture.c2GraphAlt: A line chart of frame time, flat at the 60 Hz frame interval
Architecture.c3Title: Beauty becomes luxury when it can be measured.
Architecture.c3Text: Performance, accessibility, best practices, SEO: four rings, measured on this very page. A visitor who leaves in three seconds is never won back by a manifesto, so we measure first and say it afterwards.
Architecture.c3Tags: CLS · LCP · TBT · measured, dated and sourced
Architecture.c3Detail: Desktop: CLS {cls}, LCP {lcp}, TBT {tbt}. Mobile (simulated slow 4G, 4× CPU slowdown): performance {mobile}.
Architecture.c4Title: Built for the day something fails.
Architecture.c4Text: At enterprise scale, something always fails. So the automation is built around that fact: redundant queue architectures keep events moving when one path goes quiet, and webhooks are signed and verified before anything trusts them.
Architecture.c4Tags: Redundant queues · Signed webhooks · Idempotent delivery · Bounded retries
Architecture.c4DiagramAlt: A schematic of a primary lane with one interrupted node, and a standby lane carrying the load around it
Architecture.c4Caption: A schematic of the pattern, not a measurement.
Architecture.c5Title: Joined to the systems you already run.
Architecture.c5Text: Salesforce, SAP, HubSpot and Oracle are part of the architecture from the first sketch, so leads, orders and records can move between the site and the systems your business already runs on.
Architecture.c5DiagramAlt: A schematic of a central hub joined to four systems

Showcase.label: 02 — Showcase
Showcase.title:
Four industries.
One standard of silence.
Showcase.subtitle: Restraint is the finish. Each industry speaks in its own register; the standard never changes.
Showcase.conceptNote: Production prototypes: studio specimens, not client work.

estate.title: Not a property. A stage for living.
estate.text: A residence above the Bosphorus is not bought from a screen; it is felt. A slow cinematic arrival, daylight studied across the plan, and an enquiry that reaches your principals directly.
estate.videoLabel: A glass-fronted villa at dusk, the camera moving slowly in

clinic.title: Trust is built in the first second.
clinic.text: For aesthetic, dental and longevity clinics: a composed digital reception, never a sales floor. Physician profiles and a patient-initiated appointment that guides without alarming.
clinic.videoLabel: A pale clinic corridor in slow motion, soft light moving along the ceiling

law.title: Discretion is the first thing a client reads.
law.text: For law firms, advisory practices and private equity houses: a restrained, exact presence. Practice and partner pages, a confidential enquiry, and a structure in which every word is yours to approve, because applying the advertising and communications rules of your profession is your responsibility.
law.videoLabel: A dark colonnade receding towards a lit doorway, the camera moving slowly forward

logistics.tag: Global logistics & B2B supply chain architecture
logistics.title: Nothing waits. Nothing is lost.
logistics.text: For logistics operators and B2B supply chains: redundant queue architectures that keep data moving when a lane goes quiet, an uninterrupted flow of data from order to dock to invoice, and automation that takes the routine decisions so your people can take the exceptional ones.
logistics.videoLabel: Parcels crossing a dark corridor of parallel lanes; when one lane goes quiet, a standby lane lights up and the flow does not stop

Legal.privacyIntro: This notice explains which personal data this website processes and why.
Legal.p2: If you send a briefing, we process your answers (investment band, project type, timing), your name, company and title, work email, your role in the decision, an optional one-sentence description, the language of the page and the market you chose on the entry gate, to reply to your request. The briefing is delivered to our team through [DELIVERY SERVICE: signed webhook, n8n, Gmail]. Legal basis: taking steps at your request, your consent (the unticked box you confirm before sending) and our legitimate interest in answering enquiries.
Legal.p3: Our hosting provider processes technical request data, including your IP address, to deliver and protect the site. We use your IP address only for short-lived rate limiting that blocks abusive traffic. When you reach the last step of the briefing, a bot check by Cloudflare Turnstile runs and processes technical data such as your IP address.
Legal.p4: We do not set cookies of our own. Your language and your market are chosen by the address of the page (for example “/” for English, “/de” for German, “?m=” for the market) and are not stored. We use no analytics, advertising or tracking cookies.
Legal.p5: Cloudflare (Turnstile bot check), n8n and Google (Gmail) process data on our behalf to deliver your briefing; some of their servers are outside your country. [TRANSFER SAFEGUARDS, e.g. standard contractual clauses]. Their own privacy policies apply to what they process.
Legal.p6: We keep briefings for [RETENTION PERIOD] unless a contract is concluded, in which case statutory retention periods apply.
Legal.p7: Under applicable data-protection law (for example GDPR or KVKK) you can ask whether we process your data and request a copy, ask for correction, deletion or restriction, request portability, object to processing, withdraw your consent at any time (without affecting what was processed before) and complain to a supervisory authority. Send your request to contact@syncflow.agency [REQUEST CHANNELS, e.g. registered e-mail address]. Supervisory authority: [SUPERVISORY AUTHORITY].
Legal.p8h: How we collect data, and whether you must provide it
Legal.p8: We collect data directly from you through the briefing form, and automatically as technical request data (see “Security and logs”). Your name, company, work email, role and the answers you select are needed to reply to your request; without them we cannot answer. The one-sentence description is optional.
Legal.p9: From your answers (investment band and role) the server assigns the request an internal priority class (high or medium). It is written into the subject line of the e-mail we receive so that we can read requests in a sensible order. It does not send, refuse or answer anything automatically, and no decision with legal effect about you is made by a machine. A person reads every request.
